correctness.rationale: For a product of \(N-1\) distinct Hermitian Majoranas, adjoint reversal and squaring both contribute \((-1)^{(N-1)(N-2)/2}=-1\) when \(N\in4\mathbb Z\), so \(i\Psi_v\) is exactly a Hermitian involution. Products of any nonempty subset of \(N-1\) stars have support equal to a nonempty complete-graph cut and are therefore traceless by the primary paper's Proposition 3.2. The joint-projector trace then gives every sector dimension exactly. The omitted star is dependent because the full product has empty Majorana support. The proof is analytic for all allowed \(N\); the included finite verifier is supplementary.

originality.rationale: The primary paper proves only commutation of the vertex-star products and then gives a heuristic expectation of spectral degeneracy while explicitly declining to study the eigenspectrum. Its stated raw normalization is inconsistent with its own Hermitian-Majorana convention for \(N\in4\mathbb Z\). The new claim supplies the required phase, identifies \(N-1\) independent commuting involutions through complete-graph cuts, and derives all sector dimensions by character-projector traces. Targeted equivalence and broader-coverage searches found related Majorana/tensor symmetry work but no statement implying this complete-graph sector theorem.

value.rationale: The source itself singles out these commuting stars as potentially important for the eigenspectrum but leaves the spectrum untreated. The new result converts that heuristic into the exact invariant-block count and size, while also correcting the star normalization needed to formulate the symmetry as Hermitian \(\mathbb Z_2\) labels. The distinction between exponentially many equal symmetry sectors and exponential energy degeneracy is structurally important for spectral analysis and for any later numerical diagonalization; it is not an arbitrary parameter slice or a merely cosmetic sign check.
